image_description: A close-up photograph of a high-performance automotive disk brake assembly. The image features a large, silver metallic rotor with cross-drilled holes and curved surface slots. A bright red multi-piston caliper is mounted on the right side of the rotor. The central hub area shows a complex lug bolt pattern with multiple circular openings. The background is dark and indistinct, suggesting a workshop or garage environment.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Circular metal rotor (disc), notably larger in diameter than its thickness.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The rotor is clearly circular and dominates the frame. Its diameter is significantly larger than its visible thickness, matching the description of a standard disk brake.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Caliper is cast metal mounted over rotor edge.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: A red caliper housing is clearly visible straddling the outer edge of the rotor on the right side.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Rotor is mounted to wheel hub with visible lug bolt pattern.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The center of the rotor reveals a hub assembly with a distinct pattern of bolt holes/circular cutouts typical for wheel mounting.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Rotor is ventilated (two plates with cooling fins) or solid.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: While the rotor is likely ventilated given its performance appearance, the specific internal structure (cooling fins between plates) cannot be visually confirmed from this external angle as the gap is too narrow to resolve details.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Brake pads are rectangular friction material blocks pressing against rotor faces.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Dark rectangular shapes consistent with brake pads are visible within the jaws of the red caliper, positioned against the rotor surface.
The hydraulic hose/line is obscured by the darkness of the background and the angle of the caliper; it is not clearly visible entering the caliper body.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Surface shows machined concentric grooves or cross-drilled holes.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The rotor surface clearly exhibits both cross-drilled holes and curved machined slots/grooves.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Surface exhibits heat discoloration (blue/brown tint) from use.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The rotor surface appears uniformly silver/metallic. There is no obvious blueing or brown rust/discoloration indicative of significant heat cycling or age.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Caliper is cast aluminum or iron.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The caliper has the smooth, slightly textured finish typical of cast metal components, painted red.

selected_experts.reason: To confirm the specific taxonomy class and distinguish between similar mechanical parts.
To verify the physical separation between the caliper and rotor and ensure the hub depth is realistic.
To check for melting artifacts at the boundaries of the shiny metal surfaces against the dark background.
To assess texture consistency on the metal surfaces and detect any subtle generation noise.

focus_areas: Integrity of the cross-drilled holes (ensure they are consistent depth and shape)
Boundary sharpness between the red caliper and the silver rotor
Geometric plausibility of the hub bolt pattern
Texture realism of the machined metal surface
custom_prompts_for_reflector: Pay close attention to the symmetry of the drilled holes on the rotor. AI generators often distort patterns near the edges or warp them non-uniformly. Also, verify that the 'slots' on the rotor follow a logical curvature relative to the rotation direction, rather than appearing as random scratches.
